init.title: Video source, Bluetooth fallback, schedule writes & vendor pet ids
init.description:
The feeder serves its video to one consumer only — Scrypted. Paste Scrypted's rebroadcast URL for the feeder here so Home Assistant consumes that instead of opening a second stream on the device. Leave empty to use the device directly.

If the feeder's BLE MAC is known (once a Bluetooth proxy has seen it advertise), feed commands fall back to Bluetooth whenever the agent's Wi-Fi API is unreachable. Leave empty to disable the fallback.

Schedule-card writes (add/edit/remove/toggle) are refused until you turn this on — the MCU's per-entry time encoding is still unconfirmed, so a wrong table could dispense at the wrong time or amount.

The feeder's own identifier reports the Petkit cloud pet id it was enrolled under, never a name. List `id=name` pairs (the id shows as `pet_id` on the last detection sensor) so that cat's presence sensor also follows the vendor's identification.

error.not_mac: Must be a MAC address, e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.bad_pet_ids: Each entry must be <numeric id>=<name>, e.g. 101320712=Kitty

speaker_busy.message: The feeder's speaker is already in use (another clip, or the vendor app): {error}

schedule_writes_disabled.message: Schedule writing is disabled until the time encoding is confirmed — see docs/schedule.

no_pending_face.message: No pending face to label right now.

feeder_unresponsive.title: {name} is not responding
feeder_unresponsive.description:
The feeder has not answered {failures} polls in a row (most recent error: {error}). Entities keep showing their last known values, not live ones, until it recovers.

Check that the feeder is powered on and connected to Wi-Fi, and that its `kibbled` agent is running. This resolves itself — and this issue clears — as soon as a poll succeeds again.
